title: Apply reusable presentation profiles to walkthrough outputs

fields.outcome: Documentation producers can apply an optional, reusable presentation profile that places a walkthrough on a polished canvas or inside browser-like window chrome without changing the captured application.
fields.scope: Add validated DOM presentation options for pure, background, and window modes; solid or gradient canvas colors; padding; window title; corner radius; and shadow. Preserve the current pure replay by default and make the profile available to DOM-to-WebM rendering. Exclude screenshot composition, arbitrary image backgrounds, and branded preset libraries.
fields.acceptance: A caller can select pure, background, or window presentation for a DOM replay, configure its canvas and frame, receive a responsive replay with stable controls and no clipping, and render the same module presentation to WebM; omitted presentation options preserve the existing output.
fields.decisions: Keep the replay controls outside the captured application and apply presentation only in the generated player shell. Normalize to a small serializable profile and use CSS custom properties so DOM playback and recorded rendering share one source. Use restrained defaults and keep decorative browser chrome non-interactive.
fields.verification: Add option validation and generated-markup tests, exercise pure and window modes in Playwright at desktop and narrow widths, inspect the DealDesk window-mode replay, render it to WebM, run the full package checks, and run frozen AgentHouse evaluation.
fields.dependencies: Builds on DOM autoplay capture and modular video assets. ST-12 adds motion within this presentation shell.
fields.risks: Decorative framing can reduce useful viewport space or cause nested scrolling. Keep dimensions explicit, scale the replay within an overflow-hidden stage, and test representative desktop and narrow layouts.
fields.audience: Developers, support teams, product managers, and marketers producing polished walkthroughs.
fields.changes: Implemented in commit 09c550b785a8ac7af2dcdb57887aaf5cd12bde48: validated presentation profiles add pure, background, and browser-window modes with responsive fitting, configurable canvas styling, and an exported DOM-to-WebM renderer that records the generated player in control-free render mode.
fields.evidence: The full package suite passed 84 tests, including a browser-backed presented replay, responsive overflow checks, invalid-profile handling, offline image replay, and a non-empty rendered WebM. The DealDesk example was inspected at 1440x900 and 390x844 with no page overflow. Its final border-free VP8 WebM is 1440x900, 19.12 seconds, and 2,152,297 bytes. Frozen Agenthouse evaluation for the exact build satisfied all seven configured checks.

criteria.expectation: Presentation is opt-in and existing recordDom callers retain the current pure replay appearance.
Callers can select pure, background, or browser-window presentation with a configurable title.
Solid and gradient backgrounds, padding, corner radius, and shadow are validated and rendered without clipping.
The presented replay remains usable at desktop and narrow viewport widths with stable controls and no horizontal page overflow.
A generated DOM module can be rendered to a non-empty WebM using its exact presentation profile.
Validation failures are deterministic and presentation configuration remains machine-readable for local and CI workflows.
